summary: Lobsang Sangay specializes in Tibetology. He studied at the University of Delhi (~1988–1994) and Harvard Law School (~1995–2004), later serving as a researcher at Harvard University (~2004–2011).

Working in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Lobsang Shastri served as Head Librarian of the Tibetan Section at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives (attested 2003–2006) and as Senior Librarian at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center (attested 2018).

Lobsang Tendzin is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Drepung and Gyuto monasteries under Ngawang Jinpa and the 14th Dalai Lama. He directed the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1971–2001).

Lobsang Tenpa works in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He completed a Master of Philosophy at Jawaharlal Nehru University under the supervision of Sharad K. Soni.

A scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology, Lobsang Yongdan studied at Kumbum Monastery and earned his PhD at the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger. He held postdoctoral posts at the University of Bonn and MPIWG.

Loden Sherab Dagyab specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Drepung Monastery under Trijang Rinpoche, Ling Rinpoche, and the 14th Dalai Lama, joined the University of Bonn in 1966, and founded Tibethaus Deutschland in 2005.

Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he studied at Drepung Monastery under Trijang Rinpoche and Ling Rinpoche. He directed Tibet House, New Delhi (1964–1966), served as a Tibetologist at the University of Bonn from 1966, and founded Tibethaus Deutschland in 2005.
Lodrö Chökyi Sengé studied under Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Kalu Rinpoche, and also taught Kalu Rinpoche.

Lodrö Sangpo works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, having studied under Ernst Steinkellner. He founded the Nitartha Institute in 1996 and was attested as a senior teacher at the Vidyadhara Institute in 2008.

A scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, Lokesh Chandra studied at the University of the Punjab and Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. He directed the International Academy of Indian Culture and chaired the Indian Council of Historical Research (~2014–2017).

Lopon Tenzin Namdak works in Tibetology and religious studies, having studied at Menri, Tingchen, and Yungdrung Ling monasteries. He served as lopön at Menri Monastery, founded Triten Norbutse Monastery, and held visiting posts at SOAS and the University of Munich.

Lore Sander works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, having studied under Ernst Waldschmidt. She held posts at the Museum für Indische Kunst, the Free University of Berlin, and the Humboldt University of Berlin.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies, Lori Meeks earned her BA at Columbia and PhD at Princeton under Jacqueline I. Stone. She was a postdoctoral fellow at Stanford and became Assistant Professor at USC in ~2004.

Lorna Srimathie Dewaraja specialized in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Ceylon and the University of London, later serving as Associate Professor of History at Ceylon (~1965–1978) and at the University of Colombo.

A scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and art history, Lothar Ledderose studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, Princeton, Harvard, Tokyo, and Cologne. He served as Professor at Heidelberg University (~1976–2010) and President of the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (1978–1990).

A specialist in archaeology and Sinology, Lothar von Falkenhausen studied at Bonn, Peking University, Kyoto, and Harvard. In 1993, he became a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles, and later co-founded the Journal of East Asian Archaeology.

Louis Dumont was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Marcel Mauss and Walther Schubring. He taught at the University of Oxford (1951–1955) and served as Directeur d'Études at the EHESS starting in 1955.

Louis Finot worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology, graduating from the École des chartes. He served as the first director of the École française d'Extrême-Orient (1898) and later taught at the Collège de France (1920–1930).
Louis Gabaude is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who held an academic post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient from approximately 1980 to 2007.

Louis Gernet specialized in history and archaeology, having studied at the École Normale Supérieure (~1902–1905). He held posts at the University of Algiers (~1917–1948) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1948–1962).
